subject: science
cluster: The solar system and the universe

items.prompt:
The largest object in the solar system is:
A) Jupiter
B) The Sun
C) Earth
D) The Moon

steps: The Sun is by far the largest object.

items.prompt:
Which planets are small and rocky?
A) The outer planets
B) The inner planets
C) All planets
D) No planets

steps: The inner planets are small and rocky.

items.prompt:
Which is an outer gas giant?
A) Mercury
B) Earth
C) Jupiter
D) Mars

steps: Jupiter is a large outer gas giant.

items.prompt:
Which is larger, Earth or Jupiter?
A) Earth
B) Jupiter
C) They are equal
D) Neither has size

steps: Jupiter is much larger than Earth.

items.prompt:
Why do scientists use scale models of the solar system?
A) To make it look pretty
B) Because real sizes and distances are too large to picture
C) To change the planets
D) Because models are required
items.answer: B) Because real sizes and distances are too large to picture

steps: Scale models shrink huge sizes and distances so we can compare them.

items.prompt:
Besides planets and the Sun, the solar system also contains:
A) Only clouds
B) Moons, asteroids, and comets
C) Nothing else
D) Other galaxies

steps: The solar system includes moons, asteroids, comets, and dwarf planets.

items.prompt:
A data table shows Neptune is far more distant from the Sun than Mercury. This shows the solar system:
A) Is very small
B) Spans huge distances from close-in to far-out planets
C) Has no order
D) Has only two planets
items.answer: B) Spans huge distances from close-in to far-out planets

steps: Planet distances grow enormously from inner to outer planets.

items.prompt:
In a scale model, why must every object be shrunk by the same factor?
A) To make the Sun bigger
B) So the relative sizes and distances stay accurate
C) So planets disappear
D) It does not matter
items.answer: B) So the relative sizes and distances stay accurate

steps: Using one factor keeps the proportions correct.
